title: Read AI Pricing: Free, Pro and Enterprise Plans (2026)
summary: Read AI pricing covers four plans—Free, Pro, Enterprise and Enterprise+—each with different usage limits. See the caps and features to pick the right plan.
body_markdown:
## Five plan limits teams hit


Only if the plan also covers the meetings does its price cover the break-even hours, and Read AI's limits decide that. Five of them, each set out on Read AI's pricing page or help docs, are what a small team tends to hit:


- Billing is per seat, so the monthly cost grows with every person you add (pricing page).
- The Free plan caps you at 5 meetings a month, so **the sixth meeting simply goes unrecorded** (pricing page).
- Features are gated by plan, so the summary you saw in a demo may not be on the plan you bought (pricing page).
- Retention differs by plan, so older meetings may not be there when you go looking (help docs).
- Admin and integration features are reserved for higher plans, so team-wide control costs more than team-wide recording (pricing page).


A seat is one paid person. Five people who only read notes may not need five seats, but five people who each run their own meetings do, so you need seats for concurrent users, not just headcount.


Count the people who host calls, not the people on the team.


### Feature and storage gates by plan


Uploads are the clearest example. Pro includes[100 minutes per month of file uploads, and Enterprise includes 200](https://support.read.ai/hc/en-us/articles/24730938146579) . That's under two hours of recordings on Pro, so a team that uploads a few long interviews a month will use it up fast.


Enterprise gives you a little over three hours, which is still a ceiling, not a free pass.


On Free, the 5-meeting cap works the same way: a team with weekly calls across three clients runs out before the month does, so even modest operational patterns exceed the tier immediately.


### Read AI integrations and admin controls by plan


When you need the connections that make notes useful, such as sending them to your other work tools, or the controls that let one person manage everyone's settings, expect them on higher plans.


If you need them, price the higher plan from the start. Finding out in the middle of a project costs you the notes you didn't capture.


If the connection you need is only a summary landing in Slack, a CRM or a task tracker,[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) bills 1 credit per flow run however many steps sit inside it, so a ten-step flow costs the same as the two-step shortcut it replaced.


That matters because the sound way to build it is in small, separate steps (fetch the summary, split out the action items, one step per destination), and none of those steps adds to the bill.


Zapier charges per task and Make per module, so on their pricing pages the same flow gets dearer with every step you add, while Activepieces' free tier gives you 1,000 credits a month with unlimited flows.


Add up your hosts, your meetings and your uploads, then compare them with these limits.
